title: Tension pneumothorax recognition
logic: Respiratory distress AND unilateral absent breath sounds AND (tracheal deviation away, distended neck veins, hypotension or rising airway pressures in the ventilated patient)
action: Do NOT wait for imaging: immediate needle decompression then finger/tube thoracostomy; document time and response; a chest radiograph of a tension pneumothorax is a process failure

title: Massive haemothorax threshold
logic: Initial chest-drain output greater than ~1500 ml, or ongoing loss greater than ~200 ml/hour for 2-4 hours, or physiological deterioration with continuing drainage
action: Activate massive-transfusion response and thoracotomy pathway; notify the most senior surgeon available and the referral thoracic service; do not clamp the drain to 'tamponade' the chest — clamping hides, not stops, the bleeding

title: Cardiac tamponade physiology
logic: Hypotension with raised venous pressure/distended neck veins, muffled heart sounds, pulsus paradoxus, or echo showing effusion with diastolic collapse — especially with TB history, malignancy or penetrating chest trauma
action: Emergency decompression pathway: echo-guided pericardiocentesis where skills/equipment exist, surgical window otherwise; anaesthetic induction before decompression is a recognised arrest trigger — sequence the theatre plan accordingly

title: Empyema staging drives the intervention
logic: Pleural sepsis recorded without a stage: exudative (free-flowing), fibrinopurulent (loculated pus), or organised (thick peel, trapped lung)
action: Prompt staging from ultrasound/radiograph and drainage behaviour at each review; exudative/fibrinopurulent stages route to drainage (with fibrinolytics where stocked), organised stage routes to decortication referral — an undrained loculated empyema on prolonged antibiotics is a stalled pathway

title: Chest drain safety documentation
logic: Chest drain inserted AND any of: side/site not recorded, post-insertion radiograph absent, underwater-seal check absent, or output charting not started
action: Block procedure-record completion until side, site, technique, post-insertion film and initial output/swing status are documented; schedule output charting; surface the 'never clamp a bubbling drain' advisory on the observation chart

title: Pleural and pericardial fluid must be sent for TB studies
logic: Empyema drainage, effusion aspiration or pericardial window recorded AND no TB microscopy/culture (or Xpert) request linked to the specimen
action: Prompt the ordering of TB studies plus cytology/culture on every pleural and pericardial specimen — tuberculosis is a leading local cause and a missed send loses the diagnostic window; link results to the national TB programme workflow when positive

title: Prophylactic antibiotics for tube thoracostomy in chest trauma
logic: Chest drain placed for traumatic haemothorax/pneumothorax AND no peri-procedural antibiotic recorded
action: Prompt a first-generation cephalosporin (or local-policy agent) at insertion per trauma convention, and tetanus review for penetrating wounds; continue only per protocol — prolonged courses are not indicated for the drain alone

title: Anti-TB therapy linkage for tuberculous pericardial/pleural disease
logic: TB confirmed or clinically probable on pericardial or pleural specimens AND no anti-TB regimen active on the medication record
action: Raise a start-treatment task routed to the TB programme pathway (with steroid adjunct consideration for pericarditis per national guideline); surgery drains the space, chemotherapy treats the disease — both must be on the record

title: Chest drain daily review and removal criteria
logic: Chest drain in situ: daily check of output volume/character, swing, bubbling and dressing; removal criteria = no air leak, output below the unit threshold (~100-200 ml/24 h serous), lung expanded on imaging
action: Schedule daily drain review tasks; when criteria met, prompt removal with breath-hold occlusive technique and a post-removal radiograph; flag any drain in situ beyond 7 days without an escalation note to the surgical team

title: Post-thoracic-surgery clinic and physiology review
logic: Thoracotomy, decortication, pericardial window or PDA ligation completed AND no follow-up encounter booked at discharge
action: Auto-book: wound and radiograph review at 2 weeks, functional review at 6 weeks (echo for pericardial/cardiac cases, spirometry consideration post-decortication); TB cases additionally linked to programme review dates; flag non-attendance to community follow-up
